ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L. 561-1 et seq. and R. 561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT and beneficial-ownership register framework), in particular Article L. 561-2-2 (UBO definition threshold) and Articles L. 561-45 et seq. / R. 561-52 et seq. (UBO declaration deposited with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 1er décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin 2), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Décret n° 2020-1191 du 29 septembre 2020 restricting public access to the UBO register; Décret n° 2018-284 du 18 avril 2018 on asset freezing and prohibition of funds disposal; Code de commerce Articles L. 123-1-7 and R. 123-53 et seq. on registry filings.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity card of each manager (gérant) and each beneficial owner (bénéficiaire effectif)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the holder's country of residence / certified by a notary of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin country is party to the HCCH 1961 Convention) followed by certified French translation; otherwise French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing / recent corporate extract of each non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed power of attorney (procuration) of each non-resident shareholder appointing the French signatory or gérant, including corporate authorization resolution if the shareholder is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the shareholder's country of residence or competent consular authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of deposit of the share capital (attestation de dépôt des fonds) and proof of physical address of the gérant (dated less than one month before filing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution (banque dépositaire) or French notary (notaire)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; original certificate issued directly to the notary or company registry, supported by certified translation if issued in a foreign language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the gérant, statutory signatories, shareholders reaching the 25% threshold and all other beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, French national asset-freezing measures (fonds de gel administered by Direction générale du Trésor), OFAC SDN and Consolidated Lists (market practice for USD-cleared documentary credit operations), and the domestic French watchlists; PEP identification and enhanced due diligence under CMF Articles L. 561-5, L. 561-5-1, L. 561-10 and L. 561-10-2; screening results, source-of-funds analysis and risk-rating memoranda must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship and made available to TRACFIN upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) — procedures.inpi.fr; name and trademark verification via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a French SARL must appear in the articles of association in Latin script; if the chosen name originates from a non-Latin script, it must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a certified French translation where required; the name may be a surname, place name, trade name, or an invented term but must be lawful, truthful, not contrary to public order or good morals, and must not create a likelihood of confusion with a pre-existing name or trademark protected in France; the SARL must add the words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the initials 'SARL' and state the amount of share capital in all corporate documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Crédit / Caisse (prior authorization as a credit institution from the ACPR is required)
Assurance / Assurances / Mutuelle (prior ACPR authorization under the French Insurance Code is required)
Ministère / État / République / Président (names implying an official governmental connection require prior ministerial approval)
Police / Gendarmerie nationale / Sécurité publique (restricted by public-order and criminal-code provisions)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross (protected emblem under the Geneva Conventions and French law; prior authorization required)
Avocat / Notaire / Huissier / Expert-comptable / Commissaire aux comptes (regulated professional titles reserved to members of the relevant professional bodies)
Société Anonyme / SA / SAS / SASU (legal-form suffixes that mislead as to the actual corporate form are prohibited)
France / Paris / République française (official denomination components triggering scrutiny when used in a manner suggesting public sponsorship)
Hôpital / Clinique / Université (health and education terms requiring specific administrative authorizations)

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a formal corporate-name reservation system comparable to common-law jurisdictions. Priority protection is obtained by (i) publishing the mandatory notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in an approved legal-announcements journal (journal d'annonces légales) before the RCS filing, which gives the name priority as against third parties, and/or (ii) filing the name as a trademark with INPI (protection for 10 years, renewable). If the name is rejected by the Guichet unique or the RCS clerk, the applicant should: (1) refile using an alternative name after correcting the conflict, (2) request reconsideration through the INPI assistance channel, (3) within two months of the refusal, lodge a hierarchical administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) with the Director General of INPI, and (4) if necessary, petition the President of the competent Cour d'appel (commercial chamber) or the judge of the commercial court in summary proceedings (référé) under the general rules of Code de commerce R. 123-4 and TFEU-derived procedural guarantees. Where rejection results from a third-party trademark, opposition proceedings must be commenced before INPI within two months of publication of the contradictory application under Articles L. 712-4 to L. 712-6 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle; missing this deadline leaves the applicant with a subsequent nullity action before the courts when the trademark is registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry. The registered office (siège social) of the French SARL must be located in France and may be: (i) the company's own commercial premises, (ii) the gérant's home where the activity is actually carried on there (limited to one year, renewable), or (iii) the premises of a duly licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) in accordance with Code de commerce Articles L. 123-11-2 and R. 123-32 et seq., which may host no more than five companies per 100 m² of premises. Virtual domiciliation is commercially acceptable for the trading, import and engineering of port overhead cranes because the activity does not require a French industrial licence at incorporation stage; however, if operational assembly, maintenance or manufacturing is later conducted in France, a physical establishment must be opened and notified to the register and social authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 5% within the first three years — low. The registry, tax authorities (DGFiP), social-security authorities (URSSAF) and customs administration rely primarily on documentary controls; unannounced on-site inspection may be triggered by material inconsistencies in UBO declarations, disproportion between turnover and overhead, VAT irregularities, or third-party denunciations. The registered address must allow lawful service of process and access by enforcement authorities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French legal counsel — drafting of statuts (articles of association), corporate governance pack, UBO declaration preparation and filing supervision for a SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — lump-sum formation package (EUR 1,000–1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet unique / RCS incorporation filing fee, including registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and the declaration of beneficial owners (bénéficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the legal notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) in an approved journal d'annonces légales
Registered office (domiciliation) service — first full year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 300–900 per year depending on location and lease surface)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization for origin-country documents of non-resident shareholders and UBOs (bundle of 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or competent consulate of the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention statutory per-document tariff (USD 15–60 per apostille) or consular fixed legalization fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled identity documents, corporate extracts and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (traducteur assermenté / expert près la Cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 40–80 per standard page, plus urgency surcharge)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the French pre-registration bank account, capital-deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) and preliminary KYC dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule; EUR 0–150 typical for a professional account with no foreign-exchange complications

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance support — PEP, sanctions (EU/UN/OFAC) and adverse-media screening of the gérant, shareholders and UBOs, with written risk memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 15–40 per screened subject plus fixed due-diligence report fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability and trademark pre-clearance search in France (dénomination sociale, enseigne and INPI trademark database)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — INPI database search free of charge; professional search and written opinion EUR 50–100

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), and Decree No. 2020-106 (Guichet Unique procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique (formalités.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 Form (now integrated into the Guichet Unique online filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; however, if capital is set, at least 20% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the remainder within 5 years. Capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers hereby adopt the Articles of Association of the SARL, approve the subscription of shares as set forth in the capital schedule, and confirm the appointment of the initial manager(s). FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles, and that the manager(s) be authorized to open a corporate bank account, deposit the share capital, and execute all documents necessary for registration with the Commercial Court Registry. The manager(s) are also authorized to publish the required legal notice and to file the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or private deed; legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association (Statuts) in French, including corporate name, registered office, share capital, share distribution, management structure, and operational clauses. All shareholders must sign the deed. If a notary is used, the deed is authenticated; otherwise, a private deed suffices. Ensure the Articles comply with the mandatory provisions of the Commercial Code.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders and managers
Proof of address of registered office (lease or ownership title)
Declaration of non-conviction for managers (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles, amend the clauses to comply with legal requirements and resubmit. Notarization may be required if the registry deems it necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the SARL. Deposit the initial paid-up capital (at least 20% of cash contributions) into a blocked account. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage) from the bank, which is required for registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays, provide additional KYC documents or choose an alternative bank. The certificate of deposit must be issued within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales - JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, and management details. Publish the notice in an approved JAL. Obtain a copy of the publication (attestation de parution) for the filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice, correct the content and resubmit. Ensure the notice is published within 1 week of signing the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique (formalités.entreprises.gouv.fr) - online portal for all business formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 form on the Guichet Unique, attaching the signed Articles, bank certificate, legal notice publication, and identity documents. Pay the filing fee (approx. €250). The system transmits the file to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is incomplete, the registry issues a 'demande de complément' (request for additional information). Correct and resubmit within 15 days to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Kbis Extract and Register for Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; French Tax Authorities (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the registry issues the Kbis extract (official company registration certificate). The company is automatically registered for tax and social security via the Guichet Unique. Obtain the Kbis and verify the SIREN/SIRET numbers. The company must then register for VAT and corporate income tax if not automatically done.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed, contact the registry directly. For tax registration, ensure the Guichet Unique transmission is complete; otherwise, file a separate registration with the local tax office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) - Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning, and Housing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation (Operating Authorization) or Déclaration ICPE (Declaration for Classified Installations for Environmental Protection)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition Écologique) via DREAL
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) or Authorization (Autorisation) depending on production capacity and emissions thresholds under ICPE regulations (e.g., for metal fabrication and surface treatment)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental standards: wastewater discharge limits per ICPE order (e.g., COD < 125 mg/L, BOD5 < 25 mg/L, suspended solids < 35 mg/L), VOC emissions per Directive 2010/75/EU (VOC concentration < 50 mg C/m³ for certain processes), and waste handling per ADEME guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) for the facility; structural load inspections by a certified engineer; workplace clearance from the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail) ensuring compliance with occupational health and safety standards (Code du travail).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - portal: www.impots.gouv.fr (professional portal 'Espace Professionnel', electronic filing via EFI). Central formalities portal for incorporation and registry: Guichet Unique des Formalites des Entreprises - formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs and export clearance authority: Direction Generale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) - www.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly incorporated French SARL obtains its complete tax identity at registration. Step 1: file the statutory incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique des Formalites des Entreprises, which transmits to the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Societes) and INSEE. Step 2: INSEE allocates the SIREN (9-digit national enterprise registration number) and the SIRET (establishment number); the RCS issues the Kbis extract evidencing legal existence. Step 3: the French intra-Community VAT number is automatically generated in the format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN. Step 4: the corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Societes) account is opened at the competent SIE (Service des Impots des Entreprises); annual tax returns (Form 2065-SD family) and monthly or quarterly VAT returns (Form 3310-CA3) are filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr. Alternative path for a foreign entity without a French fixed establishment: direct VAT identification application to the DGFiP non-resident VAT service, including the procedural forms (Form 13763 reference set) and, where required under Article 289 A CGI, the appointment of a French tax representative (representant fiscal), resulting in a French VAT number without local incorporation; the foreign entity must separately assess whether its commercial activity creates a permanent establishment or a taxable nexus for French corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope; Pass_Through_Eligible (limited); Tax_Exempt_Zone (not applicable). A standard French SARL is subject to default taxation at entity level under the Impot sur les Societes (IS) and is governed by the territoriality principle of Article 209-I CGI: French IS is levied on profits derived from businesses operated in France, while profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments are excluded from the French tax base unless the taxpayer obtains the optional worldwide/consolidated taxation regime under Article 209 quinquies CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box system; the relevant statutory elections are: (i) option for pass-through income-tax (IR) treatment for a maximum of five fiscal years by newly created small SARLs meeting Article 239 bis C CGI conditions (individual associates and turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million); (ii) family SARL (SARL de famille) is taxable by default under the partnership/transparent regime of Article 239 bis AA CGI unless it irrevocably elects for IS; (iii) option for French fiscal integration (integration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for a parent holding at least 95% of the SARL; (iv) patent box regime under Article 238 CGI allowing a reduced 10% IS rate on qualifying net income from patented technology and licensed intangible assets; (v) optional worldwide taxation (benefice mondial/consolide) under Article 209 quinquies CGI; (vi) VAT simplification elections including the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) regimes for distance sales and non-established sellers operating in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.note: The SARL remains a limited liability entity; the absence of a minimum capital requirement and the permission for non-resident ownership do not alter the default entity-level corporate tax treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee) - French value added tax transposing Council Directive 2006/112/EC, administered by the DGFiP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established taxable persons: EUR 0 - no franchise en base de TVA is available; registration is mandatory from the first taxable euro. For domestic French micro-suppliers, the franchise en base de TVA exemption applies up to EUR 85,000 (supplies of goods) and EUR 37,500 (supplies of services), with tolerance thresholds at EUR 93,500 and EUR 40,500 respectively. The domestic franchise is not available to foreign sellers, and a French SARL engaged in manufacturing of crane and hoisting equipment typically operates on the standard regime with monthly VAT filing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting under the reform of facturation electronique, operating through the public platform Chorus Pro and certified private platforms (PDP - Plateformes de Dematerialisation Partenaires) connected to the National Invoice Directory (ANF). Mandatory structured formats: Factur-X (EN 16931), UBL 2.1 or cXML. Timetable: from 1 September 2026, all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices and large enterprises and mid-cap companies must issue e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, small and micro enterprises must issue e-invoices. E-invoice and e-reporting data must be transmitted to the ANF within ten (10) working days of issuance (or of payment acceptance for payment-related e-reporting data). France does not apply a transactional digital stamp or real-time fiscal clearance model; instead, DGFiP performs automated, systemic cross-checking of e-invoice, e-reporting and VAT return data, with a near-real-time compliance audit posture.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.special_tva_measures: Manufactured capital goods such as port container gantry cranes are standard-rated at 20%; concessional rates (10%, 5.5%, 2.1%) are not applicable to this machinery product line. Intra-EU acquisitions, imports and cross-border movements are subject to the normal VAT logistics chain, with import VAT payable at the French frontier under Article 291-1 CGI unless postponed accounting (auto-liquidation for the importer) is contractually and legally available.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of manufactured port gantry cranes, hoisting gear and spare parts are exempt with the right to deduct input VAT (effet zero-rating) under Article 262-1-I CGI where: (i) the transfer of ownership and the right to dispose of the goods as owner passes to the purchaser; (ii) the goods are physically transported outside the European Union (EU) by the seller, the purchaser, or a third party acting for their account; and (iii) the physical export occurs no later than the end of the third month following the month in which the transfer of ownership took place. Documentation must be in the exporter's possession at the date of the VAT return on which the exemption is claimed (BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-10-10-20/30). Intra-Community supplies to EU-established taxable persons follow the separate zero-rating of Article 262-1-II CGI, conditional on the validity of the customer's EU VAT number (VIES validation) and equivalent evidentiary standards. Export-related services directly connected with the exported goods and technical engineering/design studies for exported machinery may qualify for zero-rating under Article 262-1-III CGI where the specific conditions of the BOI are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAE - Document Administratif Unique lodged via the DELTA-X customs system) bearing the MRN and evidencing physical exit from the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading (or CMR consignment note / air waybill) indicating the third-country port of discharge, final destination and consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation bancaire de rapatriement / certificat de change) evidencing collection and repatriation of export proceeds through the French banking channel
Commercial export invoice (facture d'exportation) itemising the goods, Incoterms and export destination together with the documentary letter of credit or project escrow payment schedule
Purchase order / project contract evidencing the transfer of ownership and the allocation of transport risk between the exporter and the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP systematically reconciles customs export declarations (DAE flows from DGDDI), transport instruments and inward remittance (FX) certificates against the VAT returns on which the 0% rate was claimed. The clawback and reassessment window runs three (3) years under Article L.176 LPF for VAT and Article L.169 LPF for income/corporate taxes; where customs fraud is established, the customs reprise is extended to six (6) years under Article 354 of the Code des douanes. If export proof is missing, non-contemporaneous or inconsistent, the zero-rating is re-characterised as taxable French VAT at 20%, subject to interest de retard at 0.2% per month and graduated penalties under Articles 1728 and 1729 CGI: 10% (late payment after formal notice), 40% (failure to declare / bad faith) and 80% (active dissimulation or abuse of right). Falsified or fictitious export documents attract the 100% majoration under Article 1729-1 CGI and, where customs law applies, the sanctions of Articles 413 and 414 of the Code des douanes: confiscation of the goods, a fine of one (1) to five (5) times the value of the frauded goods and imprisonment of three (3) to ten (10) years in aggravated or organised fraud cases (including export VAT carousel schemes). FX compliance: although the dossier adopts a contractual outer cap of 180 days for repatriation of export proceeds, French customs foreign-exchange discipline requires collection within the banking and contractual deadlines (commonly thirty (30) days after the payment due date under Article 153 of the Code des douanes as referenced in DGFiP/DGDDI practice); failure to repatriate within the applicable window triggers retrospective denial of the zero-rating benefit and the clawback of VAT plus interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with foreign exchange and trade reporting administration jointly overseen by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) and the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a member of the euro area and applies the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital. The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Non-resident owners may freely inject capital, service debt, and remit dividends, subject to mandatory economic substance, anti-money laundering, and sanctions screening. Profit remittance is not subject to FX licensing or quantitative limits; however, balance-of-payments declarations and tax reporting obligations apply. The only residual restrictions arise from EU/UN sanctions, anti-money-laundering verification, and documentary evidence requirements for bank execution. For foreign currency exposures, conversion is freely permissible through the interbank market, but transactions to non-account holders or on behalf of OFAC-listed jurisdictions face stringent compliance blocking risk.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France currently imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescriptive deadline for repatriation of export receipts. French exporters are required to record all cross-border transactions in their annual balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France when cumulative flows exceed EUR 15,000,000, and must supply evidence of the economic basis of any significant receivables or advance payments. Intra-EU exports are exempt from formal reporting. For extra-EU sales financed through documentary letters of credit, banks verify the underlying customs export declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU) and the financial settlement to ensure the transaction is genuine. The absence of a surrender rule means proceeds may be retained in hard currencies, but prudent treasury practice is to convert to EUR using covered forward contracts promptly to mitigate currency risk.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions licensed by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) may legally open accounts for SARL clients and provide cross-border payment services under an EU passport. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs without an EU banking or e-money licence generally cannot clear EUR-denominated payments through the SEPA/TARGET2 rails, cannot offer French IBANs, and present acute anti-money-laundering and sanctions risk. A French or EU-passported EMI is viable only for low-risk operational cash flows, collection of customer disbursements, and inward remittances; it is not acceptable for capital escrow, documentary credit operations, or high-value project disbursements due to liquidity and regulatory limits on lending and trade finance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For traditional tier-1 French banks, the manager (gérant) and any authorized signatory who is a non-resident should reasonably expect to attend an in-person interview at the French branch when opening a corporate account for an export-oriented manufacturing SARL. Remote video onboarding is progressively available at select banks for low-risk entities, but invariably requires notarised corporate documents, passport-grade identification, sworn translation of non-French documentation, and completion of ACPR-mandated customer due diligence. In practice, for an entity handling documentary credits and escrow accounts, physical presence of the managers or a delegated corporate officer is a de facto mandate for first account opening and for any power-of-attorney arrangement. A notarised power of attorney with apostille can reduce physical appearances after the initial relationship is established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity or undeclared non-resident investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official KBIS excerpt listing statutory representatives; audited or notarised shareholders' register; completed UBO declaration form identifying each natural person with more than 25% direct or indirect capital; passport copies with apostille translation; source-of-funds evidence for capital injection (bank statements from the investor's originating bank); corporate constitution and shareholders' agreement signed before a French notaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening hits on the SARL manager or UBO
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion or due diligence report from a licensed French avocat demonstrating the absence of sanctions designations; sworn justification of any PEP status; denies/political exposure documentation; negative media analysis; evidence of lawful prior business activity (supplier invoices, tax filings, trade registers); engagement letter with a French compliance advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic purpose or mismatch between declared object (overhead crane manufacturing) and fund flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed corporate business plan; executed port gantry crane sale agreements or preliminary contracts; invoices and purchase orders from counterparties; a certified flow chart linking each escrow receipt, letter of credit disbursement, and trade settlement to a specific cargo contract; declaration of the underlying commercial transaction to DGDDI; evidence of physical business premises and operational machinery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse credit history, litigation, or liquidation proceedings against the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Court extracts (extrait de casier judiciaire) for managers; a French registered auditor's report confirming solvency; declaration of no pending insolvency proceedings from the commercial court; payment default remediation evidence; an escrow arrangement assigning the incoming contract receivables as collateral to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inadequate documentary licences or regulatory permits for manufacture of port cranes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statement that the ISIC 2816 activity is not a licensed profession in France; CE conformity declarations for existing crane models; Type Examination certificates from notified bodies; ISO 9001; insurance certificates covering product liability and marine cargo risk; evidence of compliance with EU Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC and potential ATEX requirements for port zones.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound non-resident equity or shareholder loan capital is a SWIFT MT103 international wire to the SARL's €-IBAN, using the harmonised EU European Article Numbering Programme (EAN) / CF Code for balance-of-payments classification; the remitter must cite the cross-border capital transaction category under EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and the Banque de France
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard clearing rails for over/under global trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct remittances covering invoice payments; (2) Documentary Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued or advised through the bank's trade finance platform with SWIFT MT700/MT707 messaging; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR disbursements within the SEPA zone; (4) TARGET2-Ipane real-time gross settlement (RTGS) for high-value EUR wires and interbank obligations; (5) for cross-currency settlements, restricted-use correspondent accounts are used with simultaneous MT202 and MT103 pairs. For port gantry crane project contracts, banks commonly structure the outbound disbursements under a separate project escrow sub-account, with accounts payable released only upon presentation of a compliant certificate of shipment, customs export declaration, and the buyer's acceptance certificate. The SARL must ensure that all export payments are reported under the annual balance-of-payments declaration and that any pre-payment for imported components is justified by pro-forma invoices to the bank to avoid characterisation as capital flight.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable Forwards (NDFs) with ACPR-regulated European banks for transactions involving non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies
Deliverable Forwards (FX Forwards) on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH with terms up to 12 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) or FX swaps enabling exchange of principal and interest obligations on foreign-currency project finance contracts
Vanilla FX Options (puts/calls) executed through an ACPR-authorised investment firm for hedging tender or project pipeline exposures
Interest rate and inflation swaps linked to foreign-currency debt, when collateralised by cash in a French bank account

Cleared OTC trades through Eurex or other EU central counterparty when required by EMIR for non-financial counterparties above clearing thresholds, but generally executed bilaterally under EMIR exemption for hedging-only operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting (AGOA) approving annual accounts and allocating results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance; minutes recorded in the corporate decision register by the gérant; no external filing at meeting stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year end unless extended by judicial order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting prevents valid depositing of accounts and exposes the gérant to liability; continued default may be raised by the public prosecutor in RCS strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual financial statements, management report, auditor's report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Clerk of the Commercial Court) for publication in the RCS and BODACC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts by the shareholders' meeting; extended only by court order and then still within one month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers civil monetary penalty, daily coercive fine (astreinte) under the injunction procedure, and after formal notice can result in judicial strike-off from the RCS and administrative dissolution of the SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liasse fiscale (corporate income tax return, Form 2065-SD and 2050-SD schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year end: no later than the second working day following 3 May; for a non-calendar year end: within three months of the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of unpaid corporate income tax, increased to 40% in bad faith cases and 80% in fraudulent cases, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% on amounts due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of beneficial ownership declaration (mise à jour du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) following transfer of quotas or any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual calendar date; mandatory within 30 days after any change in the identity, nature, or percentage of beneficial ownership or transfer of SARL quotas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the RBE within 30 days exposes the gérant and the company to administrative and Criminal Law penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code, including fines and, for deliberate non-compliance, imprisonment of the responsible officer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at the end of the fiscal year, the company exceeds two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax EUR 8,000,000; average permanent workforce of 50 employees. Appointment is also compulsory when the company controls or is controlled by an entity exceeding those thresholds, where qualifying shareholders representing at least one-tenth of the share capital request it, or where the court so orders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under règlement ANC 2014-03 (the French Chart of Accounts), transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; consolidated financial statements of groups are prepared under IFRS as adopted by the European Union where required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation declaration. The beneficial owners must be declared in the RBE at incorporation, and the register must be updated within 30 days of any quota transfer or ownership change. At each annual accounts approval, the gérant must ensure alignment between the company records, the quota transfer register, and the RBE in order to avoid gaps during commercial court registry reviews.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres / parts sociales)
Register of Directors and corporate decisions (registre des délibérations)
Minute Book (livre des décisions de l'assemblée)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (crédit d'impôt recherche, up to 5% of qualifying expenses), innovation status (statut innovation) for preferential rates, no general statutory tax holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 - Déclaration de résultat, electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 31 March if FYE 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A; non-residents file separate return for French PE income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: €750 minimum or 0.5% of unpaid tax per month (max 5%), plus interest; criminal penalties for willful non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Traitement de la demande de relief) on impots.gouv.fr with tax residence certificate and beneficial ownership declaration
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 5% or 10% per treaty; Interest: 0% for related-party under EU directive, otherwise 12.8% reduced by treaty

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local file if annual turnover > €50 million; Master file for groups > €750 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French ESR requires adequate employees, premises and core income-generating activities in France for tax residency and expense deductibility

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate falsification of financial statements or income declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 80% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, repayment of evaded tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution, possible imprisonment and entry bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of annual corporate tax return by deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine €750 minimum or 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (max 5%), plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines and potential criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Lack of or inadequate transfer pricing documentation or arm's length pricing not respected
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back taxation, penalties up to 80% of understated tax and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for restitution and possible disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining French SARL without adequate economic presence, employees or operations in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization, denial of deductions, reclassification as non-resident and potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability, fines and criminal penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting or suspicious transaction declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million, criminal prosecution and asset freezing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, imprisonment and professional sanctions
